assets.title: Glass tide
assets.caption: Generated by Kling v3 Pro on Microsoft Foundry (fal, preview): 'Glass tide', one 5 s text-to-video clip, 1920x1080, Nov 9 2026. Continuous subject and camera motion in one take (audio off). Unmodified original download.
assets.alt: AI-generated clip: a translucent glass manta ray with blue veins glides across a green tiled hall toward a round brass doorway; the camera follows through it to a tall window over a city skyline.
assets.prompt: A translucent sea-glass manta ray, with delicate cobalt veins through its broad wings, glides through a flooded Art Deco observatory. A low side-tracking camera keeps the same manta ray centered in a medium-wide shot as its wings undulate slowly. The manta ray passes through one circular brass doorway; the camera follows smoothly through the doorway and reveals an enormous sunlit window overlooking a submerged city. Shafts of amber sunlight ripple across the glass wings and green tiled floor; tiny bubbles trail behind it. One continuous cinematic shot, graceful motion, clearly readable silhouette, no cuts, no text, no logos.

assets.title: Marble music
assets.caption: Generated by LTX-2.5 Fast on Microsoft Foundry (fal, preview): 'Marble music', one 6 s text-to-video clip, 1280x720, Nov 9 2026. Kinetic action with native generated audio.
assets.alt: AI-generated clip: a copper marble rolls along a polished wooden track past brass gears and three glass rods, then drops into a green velvet cup.
assets.prompt: A macro tracking shot follows one bright copper marble rolling down a curved walnut track inside a miniature mechanical music workshop. The copper marble strikes three small glass chimes in sequence, each chime visibly vibrating on impact, then settles into a velvet-lined cup. The camera glides alongside at marble height, keeping the copper marble sharp while brass gears turn softly in the background. Warm side light, tactile wood grain, teal shadows, playful practical miniature photography, one uninterrupted shot. Sound: the marble rolling on wood, three clear glass notes synchronized to the three visible impacts, then one soft landing; quiet gear ticks underneath, no speech and no background music. No text or logos.

assets.title: Paper city
assets.caption: Generated by LTX-2.5 Pro on Microsoft Foundry (fal, preview): 'Paper city', one 6 s text-to-video clip, 1280x720, Nov 9 2026. Two-shot continuity across a hard cut, with native generated audio.
assets.alt: AI-generated clip: a wide shot of a rainy paper city where an orange origami fox walks under a glowing paper lantern, then a close side shot of the same fox walking on a wet street.
assets.prompt: A low wide shot reveals a miniature rain-soaked city folded entirely from paper, with glowing amber windows and teal puddle reflections. A small orange origami fox with a white folded-paper tail tip steps from beneath a blue paper awning and looks up as a glowing paper lantern drifts overhead. A hard cut moves to a close side-tracking shot of the same orange origami fox with the same white folded-paper tail tip; the fox takes two careful steps and its reflection travels across a puddle while the lantern passes above. Visible folded-paper edges and handmade textures, warm lantern light against cool rain, shallow depth of field. The rain and gentle paper rustling continue unchanged across the cut, with two soft paw taps at the end; no dialogue or music. Two shots only, no text or logos.

assets.title: Clockwork bloom
assets.caption: Generated by MiniMax H3 Max on Microsoft Foundry (fal, preview): 'Clockwork bloom', one 5 s text-to-video clip, 832x480, Nov 9 2026. Timed action beats with prompt expansion disabled.
assets.alt: AI-generated clip: a brass seed on dark blue velvet splits open and turquoise glass petals unfold into a flower with a glowing amber center.
assets.prompt: A locked-off macro product shot of a single polished brass seed resting on dark blue velvet, dramatic warm side lighting and a completely uncluttered background. From 0 to 2 seconds, a fine seam opens in the brass seed and three tiny internal gears turn. From 2 to 4 seconds, translucent turquoise glass petals unfold outward from the seed into one symmetrical flower, revealing a small amber light at its center. From 4 to 5 seconds, the completed glass flower holds still while one soft pulse of light passes through its petals. Precise miniature clockwork, delicate glass reflections, one continuous shot. Sound: quiet mechanical clicks while the seed opens, a soft rising glass tone as the petals unfold, and one clear bell note when the flower is fully open; no speech or music. No text or logos.

Amber light and a small gear at the flower's center; the open flower holds near the end
missed_or_unverified: Three separate internal gears are not distinguishable (one central gear is visible)
Framing is largely static but the subject shifts and rotates slightly as it opens
The final pulse of light is not confirmed from sampled frames

assets.caption: Source-based model options for fast drafts and final-quality evaluation; not generated video or a benchmark.
assets.alt: LTX-2.5 Fast supports rapid iteration and Pro focuses on output quality; both support synchronized audio. MiniMax H3 Max Turbo and Max support text and image inputs; Max adds image, video and audio references. Kling v3 Pro supports native audio and multi-shot prompts. Check preview access, region and offering, quota, cost and terms. Live: one real single-take clip generated per model in East US 2 (different prompts; not a benchmark).

assets.caption: Official sources, retail meters, model settings, access history and the measured smoke-clip result.

live.note: One observation only (46.8 s end to end, including queue, download and ffprobe). Requires Azure sign-in, the gitignored .env, ffprobe on PATH, and sends the prompt to fal outside Microsoft facilities.

caveats: Each video is labeled with the model that generated it. Five single takes with five intentionally different prompts: not a benchmark, and timings are single observations, not a speed ranking.
Fal services operate outside Microsoft facilities; Microsoft customer agreements, DPA and certifications do not apply (Microsoft Learn). Send only benign public prompts.
Fal.EnableDeploy was registered and fal terms accepted by the subscription Owner on Nov 9 ~2:50 PM PST. This demo accepted no terms.
Catalog showed all five models in eastus2 and four (no Kling) in swedencentral; none in eastus or northcentralus.
Deployment capacity 40 means 40 requests per 60 seconds (catalog rateLimits key 'request'), not tokens per minute.

Azure Retail Prices lists 'Azure Fal' meters per '1 Second' that match the launch table (Turbo 480P text-to-video 0.025 USD in eastus2). The meters are named 'Fal Test ...' and no Kling meter was listed; confirm against the invoice.
Cost shown is an estimate: requested 5 s x 0.025 = 0.125 USD; at the measured 5.184 s output it would be about 0.13 USD. FoundryModelEstimatedCost metric was empty right after the run.
The desk smoke clip's request ID was not captured; the four creative clips record request IDs, saved immediately after submission.
MiniMax output ran 5.184 s for a 5 s request, consistent with Learn's ~0.7 s note. The clip includes an AAC audio track.
The Nov 5 launch is on Microsoft Tech Community, not the Foundry devblog.
Creative clips: one submission each, no retries or rerenders; all four succeeded on the first submission. Prompts follow fal's first-party prompting guides and were submitted verbatim.
Audio tracks on the LTX and MiniMax clips are present and non-silent by ffmpeg measurement but were not aurally assessed; no audio-sync claim is made. The Kling clip was generated with audio off.
Every creative clip missed or left unverified some prompt beats; see each asset's observations and evidence.json.
Kling cost uses the launch-table audio-off rate 0.1232 USD/s because no Azure retail meter lists Kling. Azure Monitor FoundryModelEstimatedCost was still empty after the runs.

All five published clips are unmodified original downloads (SHA-256 in evidence.json). The Kling original is 19.09 MB, above the 15 MB per-clip web budget; an optional re-encoded derivative (kling-v3-pro-glass-tide.web.mp4, 4.21 MB, SSIM 0.989) is listed under that asset's 'derivative' field. Choosing it is a presentation choice; label it as a re-encode of the Kling output.
